Minimum practice: Hold out whole source studies (or laboratories); report random-split metrics only as a reference
Why (evidence in this study): Random splits overstated accuracy about two-fold (Section 3.1)

Minimum practice: Fix a list of held-out studies before modelling and evaluate it once
Why (evidence in this study): Locked results differed from development CV (Section 3.7)

Minimum practice: Audit identical runs reported in several studies before splitting
Report per-study errors and the mean-predictor baseline next to pooled R²
Why (evidence in this study): Pooled metrics were dominated by a few studies (Section 3.7)

Minimum practice: Calibrate prediction intervals across studies, not across random runs
Support claims about effects of conditions or optimal conditions with held-out-study contrasts or rankings
Why (evidence in this study): Within-study changes and rankings did not transfer (Section 3.8)

Minimum practice: Plan 1–3 local runs in a screening design; report literature-only, anchored and local-only predictions with re-calibrated intervals
Why (evidence in this study): Three screening-design runs reduced the median error by 1.6–6.4 wt%, but local-only data were better for locked bio-oil studies (Sections 3.4–3.6)

Minimum practice: Record product-recovery solvent, yield basis, fraction definitions, mass-balance closure and reactor details in curated databases
Why (evidence in this study): Coarse parsed descriptors did not explain offsets (Section 3.2)

Minimum practice: Make code, the held-out study list and per-run predictions available (openly or on request)
